title: PM-Eng 1:1 prep - Alicia Chen & Ethan Brooks
content:
Purpose: prep for weekly 1:1 with Ethan to align on API/Console/Dedicated/Private priorities, unblock dev work, and sync on rollout timelines.

Timebox: 30-40 minutes.

High-level goals for this cycle (Q1 sprints):
- Finalize API rate-limiting config + rollout (hosted API) so we can launch region rollout by end of March.
- Console: ship per-route cost breakdown (MVP) and integrate with trace hooks for first 2 customers in beta.
- Dedicated: confirm autoscaling policy defaults and document SLOs for sales/SEs.
- Private: triage remaining install/airgap issues with KMS integration and finalize support SLA for pilot customer.

Agenda:
1) Quick sync (5m): how are you feeling re: capacity and priority? any fires?
2) API rate-limiting and routing (8m): status on ENG-1873 (token buckets, global vs regional tiers). Need decision on backoff strategy for bursty tenants.
3) Console per-route cost UI (8m): integration blockers for tracing data (PR#5123). Do we have sample payload shape for cost attribution?
4) Dedicated autoscaling defaults (6m): confirm recommended settings for committed vs burst pools; discuss canary plan for customers on Dedicated.
5) Private deployment issues (6m): KMS edge-case (customer pilot 'Acme Health') failing key rotation during upgrade; next steps and owner.
6) Action items + next steps (3m).

Notes / Status updates to bring into conversation:
- API rate-limiting: engineering implemented token-bucket perf path; observed 10% p99 latency regression in synthetic load (compare to baseline). Root cause likely locking contention in token store (ENG-1873). Ethan noted a patch that shaves lock hold time; wants to run more long-tail tests.
- Routing/backoff: product prefers soft-backoff with exponential retry hints vs hard-reject for premium customers. Need to weigh cost impact vs error surface.
- Console cost UI: frontend expects per-request trace id and token counts from runtime. Current runtime emits minimal trace; PR#5123 adds cost fields but needs schema approval.
- Dedicated autoscaling: SRE suggested default min_replicas=2, target_cpu=65, burst_capacity=20% for general workloads. Sales asked for preflight checklist to onboard dedicated customers.
- Private/KMS: reproducible failure when HSM returns 409 during rolling upgrade; Ravi believes it's ordering/race in control plane.

Open questions I want Ethan to help decide on:
- Backoff policy: do we default to soft backoff for all paid tiers and hard reject for free-tier? (tradeoffs: cost vs 3xx/5xx errors to customers)
- Rollout timing for per-route cost UI: do we gate behind the tracing rollout (2-week delay) or ship with best-effort attribution and label as "estimated"?
- Dedicated canary: can we auto-fallback a customer to hosted if Dedicated autoscaler fails? Is that safe from data isolation perspective?

Risks / blockers to call out:
- If token-bucket lock contention remains, p99 regression could jeopardize our latency SLO for hosted API in high-concurrency regions. Contingency: fallback to single-threaded token store per-tenant (worse cost) while patch matures.
- Console cost UI depends on runtime emitting token attribution: coordination risk across 3 teams (runtime, tracing, frontend). Need a short cross-team spec doc and agreed schema by next Wed.
- Private KMS issue blocks customer pilot progress; pilot may request a delay to SLA if not resolved by Mar 15.

Proposed asks (explicit):
- Ask 1: Prioritize ENG-1873 patch + long-run load test in next 48h; if p99 still regressing, we revert to conservative path for token accounting.
- Ask 2: Approve schema for cost attribution (attach to PR#5123) or schedule triage with frontend by Tue.
- Ask 3: Assign owner for Dedicated canary rollback plan (ops or SRE) and confirm feasibility.
- Ask 4: Escalate KMS 409 failure to infra on-call if no clear fix by EOD Fri.

Draft talking lines I can use:
- "We should aim for soft-backoff as the default for paid tiers - it preserves UX and reduces spuriously failed requests, and we can throttle heavier later if we see cost blowouts."
- "For the console, shipping 'estimated' per-route costs is acceptable for beta customers provided we flag the limitations and collect feedback."
- "For Dedicated canary, we should never auto-fallback a customer in a way that exposes hosted data; fallback should only be allowed for stateless routes or read-only endpoints."

Action items (to capture during 1:1):
- Ethan: run long-tail load test on token-bucket patch and share results (p50/p95/p99) - due 2026-03-04.
- Alicia: draft short schema doc for cost attribution and post to Confluence, tag runtime/frontend - due 2026-03-03.
- Ravi: open infra escalation for KMS 409 and loop in on-call - due 2026-02-27 (in progress).
- SRE/Ops: propose Dedicated canary rollback playbook and owner - due 2026-03-06.

Follow-up notes I want captured after meeting:
- Decision on backoff policy and commit to rollout dates.
- Any temporary mitigations for latency regressions.
- Final schema link for cost attribution and assigned reviewers.
- KMS escalation ticket id and next steps for customer pilot.

Scratchpad / misc:
- Quick reference: ENG-1873 (token-bucket), DED-402 (autoscale defaults), PR#5123 (console cost data), CONFLUENCE: API roadmap page.
- Slack snippets to paste after meeting: "Ethan and I aligned to prioritize ENG-1873 testing; Ethan to share results by Thursday. Alicia to circulate schema for console cost attribution - please review by Tue."

Notes to self: stay firm on timelines; if infra can't commit to KMS fix by Mar 15, propose a paid discount for pilot or delay their go-live. Keep sales/CS in loop but don't promise SLA changes without legal.

End of prep notes.
